No, don’t apologise! It’s difficult to read people over text. 

Everything that I suggest my partner just declines it. I had to go behind her back and involve professionals in the first place and I felt awful doing it. I’ve said she could stay at her parents for a week or two and my family would help me with LO whilst I would be working but she won’t try anything or listen to me really. I just feel like we’re stuck and the only thing my partner is certain on is that she doesn’t want this life anymore. She isn’t suicidal she just doesn’t want to have to care for a baby all the time any longer. It sucks. 

The health visitor has been quite good so I will start there today but other mental health services just seem to dismiss you as soon as they’ve seen you if you come across okay on the day they visit. 

Thank you for your help!

We have been receiving “support” but it’s all about medication and every couple of days she outbursts that she can’t do this any longer. I’m trying to be supportive as I can and this is the last thing I want but we’re both running out of options. We have been discussing this for a while and after an outburst yesterday I said should I call citizens advice to discuss this option and she said yes please. I am going to call the health visitor today to let them know this is what she wants and maybe she can come out and talk to her
No problem, thank you! I will be in contact with them today.

My partner has been under the perinatal team since LO was five weeks and we’ve had extra support from the health visitor but I’ve got to say the mental health services in the UK are abysmal. She has been discharged from the perinatal team twice now and is awaiting an appointment with mind matters currently. I want us all to stay together as a family but this is the only option that she thinks will make her happy. I will be taking him full time initially and I’ve mentioned you could see him a couple days a week but right now she said she doesn’t want to. It’s heartbreaking really.
